message.content:
The website is a **404 error page** for OpusClip, a video editing or content creation platform, designed with a modern, dark-themed aesthetic. Below is a detailed breakdown of its layout, visual design, and content:


### **Overall Layout & Color Scheme**
The page uses a **dark background** (near-black, `#1A1A1A` or similar) with high-contrast white text for readability. Accent colors include bright pink (`#FF3E96`), purple (`#7B2FF7`), and deep purple (`#5A1EAD`), creating a vibrant, tech-forward look. The layout is split into two main sections: a left-aligned error message and a right-aligned visual element (a mockup of the OpusClip interface).


### **Header & Branding**
- **Top-left corner**: The OpusClip logo (a stylized "O" with a film strip icon) in white, followed by the brand name "OpusClip" in a clean, sans-serif font (e.g., Inter or Arial).  
- **Top-right corner**: A vertical scrollbar (gray) indicates the page is scrollable, though the visible content is minimal.


### **Hero Section (Error Message)**
The left side of the page dominates with a bold, attention-grabbing error message:  
- **Main heading**: "Oops!" in a large, bold, white sans-serif font (e.g., Poppins, 72px), centered vertically and left-aligned horizontally.  
- **Subheading**: A friendly, conversational paragraph in a smaller, lighter gray font (e.g., 16px):  
  *"Hi there! We're excited to see you here, but unfortunately, our service isn't available in your country or region just yet. Please check out the list of currently supported countries and regions [here]."*  
  The word "here" is underlined (white) and acts as a hyperlink.  


### **Visual Element (Right Side)**
The right side features a **mockup of the OpusClip interface**, showcasing a key feature:  
- **Background**: A dark, rounded rectangle (matching the page’s background) with colorful, abstract shapes (pink, purple, deep purple, white) in the top-left, adding a playful, modern touch.  
- **Feature title**: "Auto Captions" in bold, white sans-serif font (24px), centered within the mockup.  
- **Preview images**: Below the title, three small video thumbnails (blurred) hint at the platform’s video-editing capabilities.  


### **Cookie Consent Banner (Bottom)**
A semi-transparent dark gray banner spans the bottom of the page, containing legal text:  
- **Content**: A paragraph in light gray (14px) explaining data collection for analytics, marketing, and personalization. It mentions sharing data with vendors and includes links to "Terms of Use" and "Privacy Policy" (white, underlined).  
- **Close button**: A small "×" icon (white) in the top-right corner of the banner, allowing users to dismiss it.  


### **Typography**
- **Headings**: Bold, sans-serif fonts (e.g., Poppins) for high contrast against the dark background.  
- **Body text**: Lighter, sans-serif fonts (e.g., Inter) in gray for readability.  
- **Links**: Underlined white text for interactivity.  


### **Navigation & Buttons**
- **No visible navigation bar**: The page is a static error page, so standard navigation (e.g., menu, sign-in) is absent.  
- **No buttons**: The only interactive element is the "here" link and the cookie banner’s close button.  


### **Notable Elements**
- **Color contrast**: The dark background makes white text and bright accent colors (pink/purple) pop, ensuring the error message and visual mockup stand out.  
- **Tone**: The error message is friendly and conversational ("Hi there!") to soften the frustration of a 404.  
- **Visual hierarchy**: The "Oops!" heading is the most prominent element, followed by the subheading and visual mockup, guiding the user’s eye from the error to the brand’s value proposition.  


### **Summary**
The page effectively communicates a service unavailability error while maintaining OpusClip’s brand identity (modern, tech-focused) through its dark theme, bold typography, and vibrant accents. The visual mockup subtly promotes the platform’s "Auto Captions" feature, even in an error state, and the cookie banner ensures legal compliance without disrupting the user experience.
